Subject: PoC recommendation + deployment mode next steps

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a suggested path forward so we can get a short, high-confidence PoC running next month.

Key constraints you mentioned:
- PHI-like data residency in us-east-1, cannot leave VPC without encryption and audited egress
- Expect bursts up to ~200 qps for inference during peak windows, typical baseline ~15 qps
- SSO with Okta + SCIM provisioning required for any trial with our product team involvement
- Procurement prefers a timeboxed trial (2–4 weeks) and a capped spend limit for initial evaluation

Recommended approach (proposal):
1) Two-week PoC in a Private VPC trial so we can keep data in your account while we validate throughput and latency under representative load.
2) Run a side-by-side comparison on the same model family: Dedicated capacity (Redwood-managed GPUs) vs a lightweight Hosted API fallback for non-sensitive, lower-throughput routes. This gives you both isolation and a plan for graceful degradation.
3) Success criteria (sample): p95 generation latency < 250ms for short prompts, sustained 150 qps routing capacity during peak burst tests, end-to-end integration with Okta, and no customer data leaving the VPC unenveloped.

Next steps I can start today:
- Share a PoC checklist + sample SOW for a 2-week Private VPC trial (attached).
- Schedule a 60min infra alignment with your DevOps/Cloud team and our infra engineer (Rishi) — propose Wed/Thu next week.
- Provide a preliminary cost estimate for the trial and an expected steady-state run-rate for Dedicated vs Hosted (attached spreadsheet).

If that aligns, I’ll loop in Rishi and Aditya to nail the technical runbook and booking.

Thanks —
Mina Haddad

Appreciate the summary and crisp options. High level: this sounds good and matches our bar for a PoC, but a few clarifications from our side before we lock dates:

1) Data residency: we need the inference nodes to be inside our AWS account (VPC) for the trial; we can allow minimal egress for logging if encrypted and audited.
2) Throughput: the 150 qps sustained target looks right for our primary route, but we want to validate both cold-start and sustained KV-cache performance.
3) Compliance: our security team requires a completed SOC2 questionnaire and confirmation you support customer-managed KMS for secrets.
4) Procurement: we can do a 2-week trial but need a clear budget cap — procurement prefers a single purchase order for the trial.

I’m copying our DevOps lead (devops@aurorahealth.com) so we can coordinate the infra alignment. Wed morning (PST) works for a short technical sync.

Thanks Sarah — appreciate the specifics. Short answers up front: yes to customer-managed KMS, yes to SOC2 questionnaire (attaching), and we can run the inference nodes in your AWS account as a Private VPC trial.

Concrete PoC plan (proposal for alignment):
- Scope: 10 endpoints (primary conversational route + 9 supporting routes). Controlled load test to validate 150 qps sustained and 200 qps peak bursts for a 2x30min window.
- Deployment mode: Private VPC trial with Redwood-managed runtime deployed into your account. We will also keep Hosted API routes available as a fallback behind feature flags for comparison.
- Duration: 2 weeks: 3 days staging + 7 days baseline + 4 days stress/edge-case testing.
- Success criteria (finalized with you):
  * p95 generation latency < 250ms on representative 3–6 token outputs for primary route
  * Stable throughput at 150 qps for 1 hour sustained test runs
  * End-to-end Okta SSO provisioning and RBAC for 5 test users
  * No plaintext customer data egress outside your VPC; logs encrypted with your KMS key
- Stakeholders:
  * Aurora: Sarah Coleman (AI Prod), Aurora DevOps (name TBD), Procurement (PO owner)
  * Redwood: Mina Haddad (AE), Rishi Malhotra (Infra lead), Aditya Rao (Solutions Eng)
- Deliverables: PoC runbook, test harness (load scripts), short runbook for how to revert/roll back, and a post-PoC report with comparison of Dedicated vs Hosted economics and latency profiles.

I’m attaching the sample PoC checklist and a conservative cost estimate for the Private VPC trial (see cost-estimate.xlsx). If that looks good, propose we lock the infra sync for Wed 10:30am PST and I’ll follow with a draft SOW and DocuSign for the PO cap.

Mina / Aditya —

Quick technical notes to make the infra sync productive:
- We can deploy the Redwood runtime into Aurora's account using the Private VPC pattern with an operator-managed AMI + CloudFormation/IaC bundle. For a short trial we'll recommend a 2-node GPU pool (A10G or similar) to validate latency and batching behavior.
- KV cache behavior: to validate cold-start vs warm-paths, include tests that vary prompt prefix similarity and session stickiness. We'll enable prefix caching for the primary route to simulate production performance.
- Quantization: if Aurora wants the lowest-cost Dedicated baseline, we can run 8-bit quantized kernels; for the trial keep a full-precision variant for parity testing on a single endpoint.
- KMS: confirm the customer KMS key ARN before we start; we'll need decrypt permissions for the runtime role.

I’ll prepare a one-page runbook for Wed’s sync with step-by-step deploy and test commands.

—Rishi
